slides.title: 5 clauses to check before you *sign* a creator
slides.subtitle: Most deals go wrong in the contract, not the content.

slides.label: 01 · Usage rights
slides.title: How long can the brand use the content?
slides.body: Organic reposting for 30 days is very different from paid ads for 12 months. Name the channels, the duration and the territory. 'In perpetuity' should cost a lot more.

slides.label: 02 · Exclusivity
slides.title: Which competitors, and for how long?
slides.body: 'No beauty brands for 6 months' can wipe out a creator's income. Narrow it to direct competitors and pay for every month you block.

slides.label: 03 · Payment terms
slides.title: When does the money actually arrive?
slides.body: Net 30 after posting is fair. Net 90 after the brand's approval is not. Agree the trigger date and a late-payment rule.

slides.label: 04 · Disclosure
slides.title: Who is responsible for the ad label?
slides.body: In Germany that means *Werbung* or *Anzeige* at the start of the caption, not just #ad. Write the exact label into the contract.

slides.label: 05 · Exit
slides.title: What happens if it goes wrong?
slides.body: Add a kill fee for cancelled work, a cap on revision rounds, and a fair morality clause that works both ways.
